source: Al Awad and Ivanov (2026) Loc2Repair: file-level issue localization in repo-level LLM repair
finding: Giving the repair model a file location raises the SWE-bench Verified resolve rate. Predicted locations capture about half the gain of gold locations. Time falls; token effect varies by model.
numbers: Pooled resolved rate: no localization 44.7%; predicted localization 48.9% and 49.1%; gold localization 52.4%. Mean elapsed time down 100.94 s and 52.25 s (predicted), 154.45 s (gold). Three repair backbones, two localizers.
limits: Abstract page only: models and N not named. Localization is supplied as input by a separate localizer, not made by the patching model itself. Equal-token comparison not done; tokens vary.
agent_relevance: Supports a locate step as an input to patching (gap 1), but the location came from a separate localizer. Predicted gain of +4.2 to +4.4 points is with imperfect locations.

source: Sepidband et al. (2026) RGFL: Reasoning Guided Fault Localization for APR
finding: Better file and element localization lifts end-to-end repair in the Agentless pipeline, and counterfactual injection of gold locations shows how much failure is due to location.
numbers: SWE-bench Verified (500), Gemini 2.5 Pro. File Hit@1 71.4% to 85% (Claude 4 Sonnet 75.4 to 83.6; o4-mini 68.4 to 80.8). Resolved: Agentless 258 (51.6%), RGFL file only 279 (55.8%), file+element 291 (58.2%). Of 209 unresolved: 28 file-miss, gold file fixed 14 (50%); 111 element-miss, gold element fixed 29 (26%); 175 line-miss, gold lines fixed 33 (19%); 21 had correct file, element and line yet still failed. Cost about $4.40 per sample, 3.7x Agentless.
quote: end-to-end repair performance is highly sensitive to localization quality
limits: No significance tests; baselines used different models; Python and Java only; the 12.8% headline is relative (6.6 points absolute). Gold files alone fixed 9 of 70 cases where gold elements failed, so narrowing can over-constrain.
agent_relevance: Even with perfect location, many unresolved cases still fail (gold lines fixed 19%). Location is necessary but far from sufficient. For gap 9: only 28 of 209 failures were file misses.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) SGAgent: locate-suggest-fix multi-agent repair
finding: Adding a suggestion step between localization and patching (a cause-and-fix proposal) gave the biggest ablation drop in this pipeline.
numbers: SWE-bench Lite (300), Claude-3.5-Sonnet. Full: 154 resolved (51.3%), $1.48 per instance, file accuracy 81.2%, function accuracy 52.4%. Without Suggest: 114 (38.0%), file 80.3%, function 51.9%. Without knowledge graph: 132 (44.0%). Reranking: greedy 37.7%, majority vote 40.3%, plus regression tests 44.7%, plus reproduction tests 51.3%.
limits: Paper is internally inconsistent (154 vs 152 resolved; KG drop stated as 5.3 but is 7.3). No localizer ablation. No failure breakdown by wrong location vs wrong patch.
agent_relevance: A cause-level step between location and patch helps more than location accuracy changes (localization is nearly equal with and without it). Weak LLM evidence for gap 8. Reproduction-test confirmation added 6.6 points over regression tests alone (gap 10, used as a reranker, not a false-positive count).

source: Shi, Yang and Chen (2026) From Finding to Fixing: How useful is fault localization for agentic program repair?
finding: With strong bash-only agents, supplying predicted fault locations does not help on average. It slightly lowers pass@1 in 17 of 18 settings. Gold hints help, and bug-cause hints help more than gold locations.
numbers: mini-swe-agent, GPT-5.6 Luna, DeepSeek-v4 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite. 16,248 trajectories (SWE-bench Verified 500 issues, Defects4J 854 bugs). Predicted FL pass@1 change: -4.45 to +0.40 points; none significant after Holm correction. Gold guidance on Verified (GPT-5.6 Luna): no-FL 73.4; gold file 74.2; gold symbol 76.2; bug cause 77.8; symbol+cause 80.0. Low-location-clue issues: 68.4 / 72.4 / 73.0 / 75.4 / 81.4. Gold-file reach without FL already 88.6% to 99.4%. Misleading locations: agents anchor on them in 34.5% to 100% of cases; in 40 manual Wrong-FL runs, 13 of 17 that moved elsewhere passed vs 9 of 23 that stayed.
limits: One run per setting; FL given only before repair, not on demand; gold results are oracle bounds; no dollar cost; no break-even accuracy reported. Repair-stage tokens fell 11.3% to 39.2% with gold hints, but end-to-end tokens rose in 13 of 18 predicted-FL settings (-16.4% to +129.8%).
agent_relevance: Strongest direct test of gaps 1 and 2. Modern agents find the right file anyway; an extra location step adds cost and some anchoring harm. Value is largest when the issue gives few location clues. A cause hint beats a location hint (gap 8, indirect). Suggests S5 should locate only when the task text lacks location clues.

source: Campos, Shariffdeen, Ulges and Noller (2025) Exploring generalizable APR with LLMs
finding: Moving from perfect to automated spectrum-based fault localization sharply lowers repair success across 13 LLMs.
numbers: Defects4J v3.0 Java, 100 bugs, pass@1, perfect function-level FL vs top-3 from FLACOCO: Claude 3.7 Sonnet 19.02% to 2.76%; Gemini 1.5 Pro 19.36 to 3.33; o3-mini 15.02 to 3.64; DeepSeek R1 distilled 17.16 to 0.31; Gemini 2.0 Flash 10.27 to 2.40. Correct location in top-3 for only 28 of 100 faults.
limits: Java only for automated FL; text drops (7.83 to 16.20) do not match the table. The comparison is perfect vs a weak spectrum tool, not vs no location. Failing-test information gave the largest boost.
agent_relevance: Shows that when the supplied location is mostly wrong (72% of cases), function-level repair collapses. Break-even not measured (gap 2). Do not assume self-made locations are right.

source: Coherence Collapse (2026): why code agents fail after reaching the right code
finding: Most failed agent runs on SWE-bench Verified reach and edit the correct functions but still end with a wrong patch. Wrong-diagnosis failures are a minority for capable models.
numbers: 16,758 trajectories, 3 agent architectures (SWE-Agent, OpenHands, LiveSWEAgent), 7 models. Share of failures in the right-location-wrong-patch bucket (SWE-Agent, Verified): GPT-5 68.1%, GPT-5-mini 69.1%, Qwen3-Coder-480B 66.8%, Qwen3-Coder-30B 66.7%, Qwen3-235B 64.7%, Qwen3-8B 45.5%, Qwen3-32B 37.6%. OpenHands capable models 60.8% to 67.7%. Five intermediate patches were bit-identical to gold and were later overwritten; resubmitting them passed all 5.
limits: Right location means function read and edit recall at least 0.5 against gold-patch functions, a loose test. The checkpoint intervention is an existence proof of 5 cases, not a resolve-rate experiment (ceiling 30 cases). Mostly open-weight models plus GPT-5.
agent_relevance: Answers gap 9: for capable agents, 60% to 69% of failures happen after the right location is reached. Sharper localizing addresses only the other 31% to 40%. A keep-the-best-patch rule is a cheap fix for agents overwriting good edits.

source: Yuan et al. (2025) debug-gym, tables re-read from the HTML version
finding: Re-reading the tables resolves the text-versus-table conflict: pdb from the start hurts GPT-4o-class models on SWE-bench Lite, helps strong reasoning models, and pdb enabled only after 5 failed rewrites helps every model.
numbers: SWE-bench Lite (300 tasks), mean success %, rewrite / pdb from start / pdb after 5 rewrites: GPT-4o 19.1 / 17.2 / 23.6; GPT-4o-mini 4.0 / 3.5 / 6.2; Llama-3.3-70B 2.4 / 4.0 / 4.8; o1-preview 10.7 / 30.2 / 30.8; o3-mini 8.5 / 22.1 / 19.8; Claude 3.7 Sonnet 37.2 / 48.4 / 52.1. Aider (133): GPT-4o 76.4 / 69.7 / 72.9; o3-mini 95.2 / 95.2 / 94.2. Mini-nightmare (10 tasks): Llama-3.3-70B 56.7 / 36.7 / 66.7.
limits: The text says Llama-3.3-70B is harmed by early pdb, but its SWE-bench Lite row shows 2.4 to 4.0 (tiny base, noise). Mini-nightmare has only 10 tasks and the extracted closed-model rows are garbled. Three runs each.
agent_relevance: Closes gap 4 in part: unlock the debugger after repeated failure (debug(5) is best or tied on 5 of 6 models on SWE-bench Lite; o3-mini is the exception, 22.1 vs 19.8). Early unlocking helps strong reasoning models but hurts GPT-4o-class models.

source: Wang et al. (2025) InspectCoder: dynamic analysis self repair through LLM-debugger collaboration
finding: A real debugger (pdb) beats the model simulating a debugger in its head. The gap is 8 points on BigCodeBench-R and 4.6 on LiveCodeBench-R.
numbers: Qwen2.5-Max. Resolve rate BigCodeBench-R (607 bugs): InspectCoder 67.87%, LDB block-level 64.58%, Trace-Reasoning (simulated execution) 58.32%, AutoSD 34.27%. LiveCodeBench-R (151 bugs): 12.58%, LDB 7.95%, Trace-Reasoning 6.62%. Without real debugger: 58.86% (-8.01) and 7.95% (-4.64). Cost about $0.0215 and $0.0374 per problem. GPT-4o benefits much less from dynamic information.
limits: Preprint; function-level bugs; all bugs generated by Qwen2.5-Max; only 43 patches manually verified; no tokens reported; no equal-token resampling baseline.
agent_relevance: Evidence for gap 4: real tracing beats prose simulation of execution for logic bugs, at least for a mid-strength model. Not yet tested on frontier reasoning models or against equal-token resampling.

source: Alaboudi and LaToza (2020) Using hypotheses as a debugging aid (primary text re-read)
finding: Controlled study confirms the odds ratios. Offering candidate causes (hypotheses) raised success 6.24-fold; offering fault locations did not help (1.4, not significant). A correct hypothesis early predicted fixing 5-fold.
numbers: 25 recruited, 5 piloted, 20 analyzed; 3 web-debugging tasks, 60 sessions; conditions: control, fault locations, potential hypotheses. Control: 27 hypotheses at stage 1, 3 correct (11%); stage 2, 9 of 35 correct (25%); stage 3, 15 of 38 (39%). Correct hypothesis at stage 2: 5x fix odds (p=0.01). Ordinal logistic regression: hypotheses OR 6.24 (p=0.03); fault locations OR 1.4 (p=0.64); years of experience OR 1.14 (p=0.04). Fault locations did not raise correct hypotheses (stage 2 p=0.41, stage 3 p=0.13) or fixes (p=0.67). No time difference (p=0.61). 20 of 60 sessions failed to fix; 6 of those had the right hypothesis but could not write the fix.
limits: Small N, simple web apps; the hypotheses were simulated (one correct, one incorrect) and handed to humans; the fault location was perfect. Table cells in the PDF text are garbled.
agent_relevance: Human-only. A location alone is not enough; a cause statement is. Gap 8 stays open for LLMs: no LLM study testing candidate-cause lists against location lists head to head was found (d03 and d04 point the same way indirectly).

source: Alaboudi and LaToza (2021) An exploratory study of debugging episodes
finding: Naturalistic observation of professional developers finds no single dominant debugging activity and no clean locate-then-fix sequence. Long episodes mix many activities.
numbers: 15 sessions, 11 professional developers, 30 hours, 89 debugging episodes. Debugging was 13% to 95% of session time (avg 48%). 80% of debugging time came from 25 episodes. After an edit, developers tested it 58% of the time. Logs used 70% and debugger 30% of the time when inspecting state. About 14% of episodes on self-inserted defects did not end in a fix.
limits: Public videos of open-source developers who think aloud; self-selected, small N. Does not test Vessey's strategies directly. It lists Vessey as 16 participants.
agent_relevance: Part of gap 7: modern naturalistic data show interleaving of reading, editing, testing and logging. Treat S5 phases as a loop, not a strict order.

source: Adnan and Kuhn (2025) The Debugging Decay Index (full text re-read)
finding: The fresh-start rule is supported only on HumanEval, mostly with small and mid models. Gains are largest for weak models and near zero or negative for strong ones. The no-extra-tokens claim goes beyond the reported data.
numbers: 18 models, HumanEval, six-attempt budget. Fresh start at t50 vs continue: llama3.1:8b 72.56 to 82.32; deepseek-coder-v2:16b 84.15 to 92.07; mistral 54.27 to 62.80; codegemma 66.46 to 71.95; qwen2.5-coder 94.16 to 95.12; devstral 94.51 to 93.90; codestral 89.02 to 88.41. Trigger attempt 1 to 5 depending on model. Claude 3.7 Sonnet reached 100% within about two attempts, so no fit. Tokens: only two examples (DeepSeek 108,289 to about 89,000; Codestral about 97,000 to 94,000).
quote: most models lose 60-80% of their debugging capability within just 2-3 attempts
limits: No frontier-scale or repository-level test. Text and tables disagree (six vs nine improved; 82.82 vs 82.32). Threshold not optimized. The 60-80% loss within 2-3 attempts is a fitted curve, not a measured fresh-start gain.
agent_relevance: Gap 5 stays mostly open: the rule is supported for weak and mid models on a toy benchmark only. Keep it as a cheap rule for small models; do not claim it for frontier agents on real repos.

source: Leveraging print debugging to improve code generation in large language models (2024)
finding: Letting GPT-4 insert print statements and read the logs beat rubber-duck explanation on LeetCode, with a larger gain on harder problems.
numbers: GPT-4, LeetCode set. Gain over rubber-duck debugging: 1.5% on easy and 17.9% on medium problems (absolute or relative not stated in the abstract).
limits: Abstract only. Single model, self-collected data, no equal-token baseline, no real debugger.
agent_relevance: Supports gap 4 for logic bugs: real execution feedback helps more as difficulty rises. Weak evidence on its own.

source: CogniGent (2026) Improved bug localization with AI agents leveraging hypothesis and dynamic cognition
finding: A multi-agent bug localizer that forms and tests hypotheses (causal reasoning plus call-graph root-cause analysis) beat six baselines at report-level localization.
numbers: 591 bug reports. MAP up 23.33% to 38.57% and MRR up 25.14% to 53.74% over baselines at document and method level; significance tests reported.
limits: Abstract only: models, ablations and baselines not read. It is bug-report localization (retrieval), not patching. Relative gains.
agent_relevance: Hypothesis-driven localization is the LLM analogue of Vessey's hypothesis-keeping experts (gaps 7 and 8). Not tested as cause lists vs location lists.

source: Whalley, Settle and Luxton-Reilly (2023) A think-aloud study of novice debugging
finding: A modern think-aloud study of three students links success to comprehension, evidence-based activities and methodical workflow, and failure to lack of sustained effort and precision.
quote: Lack of sustained effort, precision, and methodical processes negatively impact debugging effectiveness.
limits: Only the Crossref abstract summary was read, not the full paper. Novices, N=3, so it does not test Vessey's expert findings.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open: no modern expert think-aloud or eye-tracking replication of Vessey's breadth-first, hypotheses-kept-open result was found in this pass.

source: TraceProbe (2026) What resolve rate hides: trajectory structure diagnostics for coding agents
finding: On 2,500 SWE-bench Verified trajectories, choosing the right file is too coarse to tell success from failure. Function choice and completion behaviour separate them. Search loops are the most stable failure signal.
numbers: 2,500 trajectories, 5 production settings, 9-type action taxonomy. No rates in the abstract.
agent_relevance: Supports gap 9: file-level location does not separate success from failure. A check for search loops belongs in S5 and S6.

source: Xia, Bao, Lo and Li (2016) Automated debugging considered harmful considered harmful (metadata only)
finding: Title and DOI confirmed via Crossref. Full text and the 11.38 vs 26.45 minute numbers were not re-opened. Parnin and Orso full text could not be fetched (404 on the author site, 403 on ACM).
limits: Gap 6 stays open on primary text. Unverified reading: Parnin and Orso used students and rank inspection; Xia used professionals and large real bugs.
agent_relevance: Do not cite the two as settled; keep status contested.

source: Aligning the objective of LLM-based program repair (D4C, ICSE 2025), search snippet only
finding: A search snippet says direct debugging of the whole function beats the localize-hunk-then-repair workflow on Defects4J. Not opened.
agent_relevance: If confirmed, a counter to gap 1: direct whole-function repair can beat a locate-first pipeline.
